newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - May 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - May 15.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- Top executives of the Independent Broadcasting Authority (IBA), who were grilled by Parliament's public accounts committee on Wednesday, were likely to be axed, committee members said.

- New Africa Investments (Nail) and Rembrandt are in negotiations to take control of Gold Fields of SA (GFSA), the world's third-largest gold producer, in one of SA's most significant black empowerment deals, estimated at more than 1 billion rand.

- The cabinet has approved legislation which will change the face of the taxi industry by creating a code of conduct, a national register for taxis and mechanisms to punish associations which break the rules.

- National Party (NP) leader FW de Klerk has denied that pre-1994 governments ordered the murder of anti-apartheid activists, despite being confronted by the truth commission with a state security council document apparently calling for elimination of opponents of the state.
BUSINESS REPORT

- New Africa Investments (Nail), the black empowerment investment company headed by Cyril Ramaphosa, is poised to take a stake in South Africa's second largest mining house, Gold Fields (GFSA), Jonty Sandler, Nail's managing dirctor, said on Wednesday.
- Amcoal and Anglo American natural resources stablemate Minorco said on Wednesday they intended to buy a joint 50 percent stake in the Cerrejon Centrale coal operation in Colombia.

- Jonathan Ackerman, the youngest son of retail magnate Raymond Ackerman, has been appointed general manager of 7-Eleven Africa, the newly formed joint venture betweeen Pick n Pay and 7-Eleven Corporation.
- Roy Andersen, the former president of the JSE, has been formally appointed as the group managing director and chief executive of Liberty Life Association, South Africa's third-largest life assurer.

- Tony Katsapas, who has been embroiled in a three-year legal action alleging his unfair dismissal against his former employer, Liberty Life, was forcibly expelled from the life assurer's annual meeting on Wednesday for venting his grievances.
SAKE BEELD
- Anglo American Coal Corporation (Amcoal) is taking a 25 percent interest in a coal project in Colombia for about 145 million dollars (650 million rand).
- Telkom's foreign strategic equity partners are going to support a five-year training programme at a cost of almost 2,3 million rand.
- Tito Mboweni, Minister of Labour, is going to have to appear before the Labour Court to explain alleged discrimination against whites.
THE STAR
- Johannesburg's Wall of Remembrance has touched a nerve among the citizens of Greater Johannesburg.

- NP leader FW de Klerk told the Truth and Reconciliation Commission on Wednesday that he did not apply for amnesty because he did not believe it to be the right way to express his sorrow and remorse.
- President Mandela's eleventh-hour effort to bring Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila together to avert a military takeover of Kinshasa collapsed last night.
- A consortium led by Johannesburg stockbroker Ed Hern plans to develop a 600-700 million rand casino resort in the Kromdraai valley, the most famous of South Africa's prehistoric-man sites.
